constraints: RULED BEHAVIOUR CHANGE (Ruling D33). The ruling is recorded in the notebook BEFORE the implementation, and precedes it in the commit order.

RULING D33, COMMITTED VERBATIM: 'Ruling D33 — the implement node revises its own prior artifact; it does not regenerate. On every iteration after the first, run_implement must receive the previous iteration implement.summary verbatim, and its instruction must change from producing an implementation to revising one: preserve what the criteria judged correct, and change only what the diagnosis and the unmet criteria require. Passing the artifact while leaving the instruction as produce is not this ruling and does not test it, because a model told to produce will regenerate regardless of what it is shown, and a failure under that condition would be a false negative that misdirects to the expensive remedy. Rationale: run_implement carries no prior-artifact parameter, so the fixer never sees the artifact containing the failure it is told to fix; the instruction to address a specific value is unactionable when the artifact containing that value is not in the prompt. The measured consequence is a fresh generation and a new roll of the consistency dice, which is the observed re-introduce-the-same-class behaviour. This is a behaviour change and it is ruled here.'

FIRST, VERIFY AVAILABILITY, not just the signature: confirm the previous iteration's implement.summary is still present in state.outputs when iteration 2's implement phase runs. If the loop clears or overwrites outputs between iterations, say so — the fix then needs state to carry the artifact forward, and that is a larger change than this command describes.
ITERATION 1 IS UNCHANGED. There is no prior artifact and no revision instruction on the first pass. Assert this.

THE REVISION INSTRUCTION MUST BE EXPLICIT about preserving what passed, not only about fixing what failed. A vague revise encourages a rewrite. State the instruction you implemented, verbatim, in the response.

The existing diagnosis fields are already correct and complete — red_cause, per-criterion validate_evidence, unmet_criteria, review_findings, resolution_directive. Do NOT change them. This ruling adds one input and changes one instruction; nothing else moves.

REPORT THE PROMPT-SIZE DELTA: the artifact is prose and is now added on every iteration after the first. Report the input-token increase per iteration at the observed artifact size. If the artifact can be large enough to threaten a context limit, say so and state the limit — do not silently truncate.
Do NOT change the model, the tier, any threshold, any bound, any gate, or any other phase. This is a prompt-shape change on one node.

Provider-free test: assert iteration 1's prompt carries no prior artifact, and iteration 2's prompt carries the prior artifact verbatim plus the revision instruction. Prove it by breaking it — remove the artifact and show the assertion fail (convention 22).
Do NOT run anything paid in this command. The discriminating run is its own command.
Keep the diff small. Suite reported before and after.

questions: Is the artifact available at iteration 2, or cleared between iterations? This is the precondition that decides whether D33 is a prompt change or a state change.

Should the revision instruction name the specific criterion and value, given the artifact is now present — 'line X states kappa=17.99 against your threshold 17' — or stay generic and let the model locate it? Naming it is more likely to produce a local edit, but it presumes the diagnosis identified the location, which validate may not have.
